title: Aleppo Oak: Ancient Aleppo Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Cyprus's form of the gall oak. The largest, at Laneia, is 8.4 metres round; another has stood by frescoes dated 1192 for seven or eight centuries.
intro: The Aleppo oak, Quercus infectoria subsp. veneris, is the Cyprus form of the gall oak of the eastern Mediterranean, and all four of ours stand on the island. The oak specialist who toured Cyprus for the International Oak Society in spring 2026 called the one on the Akamas peninsula, where the Aphrodite and Adonis trails fork, the most impressive he met, with a trunk about two metres across and no age anyone has written down. The oak of Laneia, in the wine hills above Limassol, is 8.4 metres round by two observers' tapes, though the forestry register says 6.10. At Lagoudera an oak put at seven or eight centuries, both figures estimates, stands in the yard of Panagia tou Araka, whose frescoes are dated 1192. And in Pano Platres the same specialists know one simply as Cyprus 505, after its girth in centimetres.
